transcript.text: f/f freezer keeps icing up bottom drawer wont shut proper, defrosted it 2wks ago already full of ice again. indesit

It sounds like your Indesit fridge-freezer is suffering from a defrost issue. Since you've already manually defrosted it and the ice has returned within two weeks, this usually points to one of two things: either the automatic defrost system (heater or sensor) has failed so the ice never melts away naturally, or the drain hole that carries that meltwater away is blocked, causing water to refreeze at the bottom. To narrow it down, please switch off and unplug the appliance. Once the ice has fully melted, check the small drain hole at the bottom of the back wall inside the freezer compartment. Is this drain hole currently blocked with debris or ice, or does it look clear?
its a static freezer, no auto defrost i think. not sure bout a drain hole at the back. but the door seal looks dodgy at the bottom corner, split bout 5cm

[Heading: Failed door seal]
That 5cm split in the bottom corner of the seal is almost certainly the cause. In a static freezer, warm air leaking in through that gap will condense and freeze rapidly at the coldest point (the back/bottom), which explains why the ice has returned so quickly despite your manual defrost. The drawer won't shut properly because the ice buildup is physically blocking it or the door isn't sealing tight enough to close fully. To fix this, you will need to replace the freezer door seal. Since you have a static model, there are no complex electrical defrost parts to worry about—just the rubber gasket. You can buy a replacement seal online using your Indesit model number (usually found on a sticker inside the fridge or on the frame). Once it arrives: 1. Unplug the appliance.
2. Remove the old seal: usually, it is held in by a retaining strip or screws along the door edge. Gently pull out the old rubber.
3. Clean the groove thoroughly.
4. Fit the new seal, ensuring it sits evenly and the corners are tight (do not stretch it).
5. Plug it back in and check that the door closes firmly with no gaps. If you can't find the exact model number on your sticker, let me know what other labels or numbers you see, and I can help you identify the right part.
ok will go read the rating plate, its IB55532W indesit. what do i search for to get the right seal, and is it push-in or screwed? i'll have a closer look at it

[Heading: Split door seal (gasket)]
For the Indesit IB55532W, search for "Indesit IB55532W freezer door seal" or use a parts catalogue with that model number to find the exact gasket. On this type of static fridge-freezer, the seal is typically held in by a plastic retaining strip (push-in) rather than screws, though you should check your specific unit once you have the new part. To remove it, look for a thin plastic or metal channel holding the rubber in; gently pull out the old seal and its retaining strip, clean the groove thoroughly with warm soapy water, then fit the new seal (and strip) ensuring it sits evenly without stretching. Once fitted, plug the appliance back in and check that the door closes firmly.
